newsitem.title: USA: Calif. plans $1 billion school computer initiative.
newsitem.headline: Calif. plans $1 billion school computer initiative.

text.p: Gov. Pete Wilson proposed a $1 billion, four-year initiative Monday to increase computer technology in California schools.
The initiative would provide $500 million in state funds over four years, with a local match requirement doubling its value to $1 billion, Wilson's office said.

Wilson's proposed budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year starting July 1, to be unveiled later this week, will include $50 million in first-year funding for the initiative, his office said. The budget needs state legislative approval.

"Over the next four years we'll add anywhere from 400,000 to 1 million new machines, depending on how many schools participate and what they choose to do," Wilson said in a speech at Del Campo High School in Fair Oaks, near Sacramento.
To earn a grant from the state, a school must find matching funds and commit to installing the computers within two years, Wilson said.

Wilson said his proposed budget would include another $10 million for authorized computer donation programs such as the Detwiler Foundation which helps upgrade and refurbish computers and places them in California classrooms.
California's Silicon Valley is home to many of the world's leading high-tech firms, yet California ranks 45th out of 50 states in student access to computer technology, Wilson's office said.
A task force that examined the problem recommended last year that nearly $11 billion should be spent over four years to put California schools in the fast lane of the information superhighway.
